ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a Nyquist plot on complex-plane axes, with the horizontal axis labeled Re and the vertical axis labeled Im. The plotted curve is an oval-like closed loop with direction arrows, and it winds once around the origin, i.e., around the intersection of the Re and Im axes. Reasoning: The problem states that G(s) is stable, so G(s) has no right-half-plane poles: P_RHP = 0. For the Nyquist plot of G(s), applying the argument principle about the origin counts zeros minus poles in the right-half plane, not encirclements of -1. Since the curve has a nonzero encirclement of the origin and there are no RHP poles to account for that encirclement, G(s) must have a right-half-plane zero.

Use the phase/winding interpretation of non-minimum-phase systems: a stable transfer function with such a net winding about zero must contain a right-half-plane zero.
